question.text: A company declares a 60% dividend on shares with a face value of Rs.2 each. If the current market price is Rs.80, what is the dividend yield?

explanation.text: The Logic: Dividend per share = 60% of FV Rs.2 = Rs.1.20. Dividend yield = (Dividend per share / Market price) × 100 = (1.20 / 80) × 100 = 1.5%. Dividend yield measures the cash return on the current market investment, not the nominal percentage on face value. The Trap: Candidates may confuse the 60% dividend rate with the yield itself. The 60% is on face value, but yield is always calculated on market price. Also, some may use only Rs.1 instead of Rs.1.20 (forgetting that 60% of Rs.2 = Rs.1.20, not Rs.1.00).
